client-registration:
The 
registering user and the end user of the registered client application MAY be different persons.
document-sharing-metadata:
In all forms the Document Source MAY add an identifier, e.g. the GLN of a healthcare professional, the OID of an
institution or the EPR-SPID of the holder: in form 1 in `author.identifier`, in form 2 in `practitioner.identifier`
and `organization.identifier` of the contained PractitionerRole, see the example
[document provided by a clinical archive system](DocumentReference-DocRefPdfProvidedByArchive.html)
([Provide Document Bundle](Bundle-BundleProvideDocumentByArchive.html)), and in form 3 in `identifier` of the
contained Practitioner and Organization.
index:
The key words *MUST*, *MUST NOT*, *REQUIRED*, *SHALL*, *SHALL NOT*, *SHOULD*, *SHOULD NOT*,
*RECOMMENDED*, *MAY*, and *OPTIONAL* in this document are to be interpreted as described in
[[RFC2119](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2119.txt)].
iti-119:
The AHVN13 (social security number) of the patient MAY be provided as an identifier with the system
  `urn:oid:2.16.756.5.32`, in addition to the minimal demographics (name, gender, birth date), see
  [Retrieve the EPR-SPID of a patient known by its social security number](iti-pdqm.html#retrieve-the-epr-spid-of-a-patient-known-by-its-social-security-number).
iti-20:
Where the main user is a healthcare professional or a technical user, the institutions or groups the main user is a
member of MAY be recorded in further agents (`agent[group]`), each with its OID and name: the groups conveyed in the
access token, or only the one on whose behalf the main user acts where that is known, e.g. the provider institution of
a document which is provided, replaced or purged.
iti-67: The Document Consumer MAY use the `full-text` search parameter.
iti-71: An Authorization Client MAY redirect the user to this endpoint to start the User Authorization.
The user MAY revoke the authorization of a primary system or digital health application at any time.
iti-72: The Resource Server MAY delegate the access decision to a policy enforcement service.
iti-81: The Patient Audit Consumer MAY use `_sort`.
openid-connect:
Certificate Authority - Identity provider MAY operate a managed Certificate Authority (CA) that is 
operated according to documented processes detailed in a Certificate Policy (CP) and Certificate Practice
Statement (CPS).

They MAY 
use this Certificate Authority to issue client certificates (mTLS) for Relying Parties.

Identity providers 
MAY delegate the service to other providers on a contractual basis.

This step MAY be omitted if the Relying Party application is a confidential client as defined in the OAuth specification and the user's consent is stored in a policy or after the initial authorization.

The Identity Token MAY contain a session identifier in a *sid* attribute, if the Identity Provider 
supports per session logout.

Identity Providers MAY provide other identity claims as defined in 
the [OpenID Connect 1.0 Core](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html) specification.

This 
Certificate Authority (CA) MAY be operated by the Identity Provider or MAY be delegated by the Identity Provider 
to a provider on a contractual basis.
volume3:

request as well
